rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a poorly expanded blastocyst with indistinct/degenerative ICM and sparse irregular TE consistent with 1DD. Minor overreach in describing vacuolation/damage not clearly discernible and limited comment on zona pellucida.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, sperm parameters, endometrium, diagnosis, and first-cycle status well, and appropriately contrasts favorable patient factors with very poor embryo morphology. Some speculative links to oocyte/fertilization issues are not strongly supported by available data.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent: severe ICM/TE compromise drives very low implantation despite favorable patient factors. Slight overstatement that such embryos are generally non-viable and recommendation against transfer is stronger than the evidence alone supports.

Mostly consistent with Gardner grading and general IVF practice, but advising strongly against transfer and suggesting many clinics would not transfer a 1DD embryo is somewhat overstated; some future-cycle suggestions (PGT-A, oocyte activation, DHEA) are not clearly indicated from this single case.

Provides clear counseling points, transfer decision framing, and future-cycle review steps. Recommendations are practical, though some are broad or speculative rather than tightly tailored to this specific first-cycle unexplained infertility case.
